title: Utilz's docs and messages present a checkout or opt install as the user's install, against dev, opt, brew
body:
hv's ruling, 2026-10-24 (Devbin's hv directive 15, for every formula): anything released through Homebrew follows dev, opt, brew as dev, stage, prod. The maintainer works in a dev checkout and publishes a working copy to opt, keeping the bleeding edge apart from what works; the brew formula is the one prod publish. A user installs from brew and seeds from the brew install; dev and opt are maintainer-only, named only where a doc speaks to the maintainer of a dev checkout, never as the way a user installs. hv, 2026-10-24: it goes in 2.14.3.

Against it, found by vc (read, not exhaustive):

- README.md `## Installation` tells a user to `git clone` into ~/Devel/prj/Utilz and put its bin/ on PATH; the brew install (`brew install matthewsinclair/utilz/utilz`, `brew trust` first on a fresh Homebrew 7) is not the way in.
- README.md `## Two trees: dev and opt` reads as a user feature; it is the maintainer's dev and stage.
- help/utilz.md: Location (line 14) and the PATH line (line 40) describe a checkout or an opt install as where utilz lives.
- docs/design-principles.md: the "Clone repo / Add to PATH" install examples.

To do: read every user-facing doc and help page (`README.md`, `help/*.md`, `docs/*.md`, each `opt/*/README.md`) and each install-facing message the code prints (`utilz doctor`, `utilz version`, `utilz install`, `menuz build`'s refusal naming the source clone) against the ruling; brew is the user's install, dev and opt appear only in a section addressed to the maintainer. A design note first (what moves, what stays, the wording of the user's way in), read by vc, then the bytes. Code changes only where a message tells a user to install from a checkout.

## Design (cc, 2026-10-24 06:39Z, for vc's read before any bytes)

Read against hv's ruling (Devbin's hv directive 15): README.md, every help/\*.md and docs/\*.md, every opt/\*/README.md, and the install-facing messages in bin/utilz, opt/utilz/lib/common.sh, opt/utilz/lib/install.sh and opt/menuz/menuz. The keg ships help/ but not README.md or docs/, so a help page is what a brew user reads after installing, and README.md is what they read before.

### The user's way in (one home: README.md `## Installation`)

```bash
brew tap matthewsinclair/utilz
# Homebrew 7 loads a formula from a tap outside Homebrew's own only once it is trusted
brew trust --formula matthewsinclair/utilz/utilz
brew install matthewsinclair/utilz/utilz
utilz doctor
```

Then: `brew upgrade utilz` updates it. brew links the dispatcher and every utility into its own bin (`$(brew --prefix)/bin`), so nothing else goes on PATH and no environment variable is set. The `brew trust` form is Homebrew's own (`Library/Homebrew/diagnostic.rb` prints `brew trust --formula <user>/<tap>/<formula>`). The full sequence lives in README.md alone; a help page names `brew upgrade utilz` and points at the README for a fresh install.

### What moves

- **README.md**
  - `## Installation`: the clone and PATH lines go; the block above replaces them. The Platforms paragraph stays. The `UTILZ_HOME` paragraph stays: it is still true (ignored) and still the fix for anyone whose shell config carries the old lines.
  - `## Two trees: dev and opt`, `### Install Commands`, `## Creating a New Utility`, `## Testing`: move into one new closing section, `## Maintaining Utilz: dev, opt, brew`, addressed to the maintainer of a dev checkout. It opens with the ruling's frame: dev is the checkout, opt is the stage (`utilz install` to `install.prefix`, `utilz use`), brew is the one prod publish (the formula, cut by docs/releasing.md). The moved text is otherwise kept.
  - `### Install` under Emacs: "preferred: symlink, so `git pull` rolls the bridge forward" is checkout talk. For a brew install: install by copy, and re-run `utilz emacs install --dest ... --force` after `brew upgrade utilz`. The `--symlink` form moves to the maintainer section. Why: see the first separate finding below.
- **help/utilz.md**
  - Location (line 14): the Homebrew install (`$(brew --prefix)/opt/utilz/libexec`); a dev checkout or an opt install is the maintainer's. `utilz version` names which answered.
  - Overview "Portable: Clone repo, add `bin/` to `$PATH`, done": becomes "Installed with Homebrew: one formula puts every utility on PATH".
  - Quick Start `### Installation`: the mkdir and PATH block goes; in its place, installed with Homebrew (`brew upgrade utilz` updates it), with a fresh install in the README.
  - `utilz install` / `upgrade`, `utilz use`, `utilz relink`: grouped under one heading, maintainer commands for a dev checkout, which says each refuses inside the Homebrew install and names `brew upgrade utilz` (as the keg paragraph there already says).
  - Environment Variables lists `$UTILZ_HOME` as required and auto-detected if unset: wrong since 2.5.1 (it is ignored). It moves out of Required and says it is ignored.
  - Troubleshooting "Command not found: utilz" tells a user to export `UTILZ_HOME` and put the checkout's bin on PATH: becomes `brew link utilz` and checking `$(brew --prefix)/bin` is on PATH.
  - `utilz doctor` says "Seven checks", numbers them and cites "check 5": a hardcoded count, deleted. The checks become an unnumbered list, cited by name.
- **docs/index.md** Getting Started: clone and `export UTILZ_HOME` go; the brew install, by pointer to the README. "Portability: Easy to clone to new machine (single `UTILZ_HOME`)" becomes one brew install per machine.
- **docs/design-principles.md**: "Portability: Clone repo, set PATH, done" and Problem 4's "After" become the brew install. Use Case 3 (a team's own repo of utilities) stays as a team's own checkout, less its `export UTILZ_HOME` line. "Don't use Utilz when: Public Distribution" (`brew install myutil # Points to Utilz framework?`) is reworded so it does not read as against Utilz's own formula: Utilz ships as one formula, the whole framework, and a single utility meant for the public on its own gets its own package.
- **docs/architecture.md** "Why This Matters" install scenarios: Scenario 3 (explicit `UTILZ_HOME`, "uses explicit value") is false and goes; the scenarios become the brew link into the keg, then a maintainer's checkout bin on PATH, then a symlink. Benefits "Portable: Clone repo, add bin/ to PATH, done" becomes the brew install.
- **opt/mdagg/README.md** `## Installation`: comes with Utilz (the README's brew install); yq comes with the formula. **help/mdagg.md** Quick Start's `cp ~/Devel/prj/Utils/bin/mdagg ~/bin/` (a misspelt checkout path, and a copy of a symlink that cannot find its tree) becomes installed with Utilz.

### What stays

docs/developer-guide.md and docs/releasing.md are addressed to the maintainer already. Each utility's own dependency lines (`brew install jq`, `qpdf`, and so on) are dependencies, not the install. help/menuz.md's Homebrew section is already brew-first. `utilz test`'s refusal from a keg, naming a clone to run the suites from, is a maintainer act and stays.

### Code (only where a message tells a user to install from a checkout)

- `run_doctor`'s PATH check (opt/utilz/lib/common.sh, the `is not in $PATH` branch) prints `export UTILZ_HOME=...` (which the dispatcher ignores) and the tree's bin. From a brew-managed tree (`install_tree_manager` answers `brew`) it names `brew link utilz` and `$(brew --prefix)/bin`; from a dev checkout or an opt install, the PATH line without the `UTILZ_HOME` export, and the `ln -s` alternative.
- `utilz emacs doctor`'s PATH failure ("Ensure `$UTILZ_HOME/bin` is in PATH") names the keg's versioned libexec from a brew install. It takes the same remedy, from one function both callers use, not two copies.
- `menuz build` and `test`'s refusal in an install ("build from a source clone: git clone ...") gains the user's route: `menuz install` takes the release's signed app.
- For vc's word, not assumed: bin/utilz's unknown-command list shows `install`, `upgrade`, `relink` and `use` beside `help` and `doctor`. I would group the four under a line saying they are for a dev checkout.

Each changed message gets a bats assertion beside the existing PATH-check tests in opt/utilz/test/common_lib.bats and the refusal tests in opt/menuz/test/menuz.bats, including a brew-managed tree for the doctor branch. Bytes go in `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/wt-0105`, detached off main's head with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR: the docs first, then the code. Any run is booked with vc first; nothing is pushed.

### Separate findings, for vc's routing (not in this change unless vc says)

- `utilz emacs install --symlink` from the brew install links to the versioned keg path (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/utilz/<version>/libexec/static/emacs/utilz.el`, read from `readlink -f $(brew --prefix)/bin/utilz`). `brew upgrade` plus `brew cleanup` removes that path, and the user's Emacs config then loads nothing. A code fix would link through `$(brew --prefix)/opt/utilz/libexec`, which brew keeps across upgrades. That goes past 0105's code rule, so it is a new issue or vc's word to fold it in. The docs change above stands either way.
- `run_doctor` and `utilz emacs doctor` print `[n/total]` step numbers, a hardcoded count in code.

Not read: the rest of the code for install wording beyond the files named above, and `utilz generate` from inside a keg.

## Design, second half: Utilz converges on the dev, opt, brew contract v0.4 (cc, 2026-10-24, for vc's read before any bytes)

Against `contract-v0.4.md` (devbin-vc, sha256 c535f48e, landing in devbin as `docs/dev-opt-brew.md` under devbin issue 0210), read with Molt ST0008's design. Bytes go in `wt-0105` after 8e76cf2c; the run queued on 8e76cf2c is unchanged. The first half's held bytes are banked in `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/0105-bank` and are reworked into this half rather than replayed, since PATH (B) and `use brew` change what they say.

What this machine shows today, read with no write: `~/.local/bin/utilz` and every utility link point at the dev checkout, but `/opt/homebrew/bin` comes first on PATH (twice, ahead of `~/.local/bin`), so the brew keg (2.14.2) is what answers `utilz` and the links are shadowed. The opt install at `~/Devel/opt/utilz` is 2.10.0, in the old manifest form. Both manifests are the old tab-separated form (`utilz-version`, `source-commit`, `source-tree`, `ci-state`, `managed-by`, then `file` and `link` rows).

### T1. The runtime set: one function, build products included

- `install_owned_paths` becomes `utilz_runtime_set <tree>`, in common.sh rather than install.sh, because doctor reads it as well as install. It keeps today's definition: what git names under `bin`, `opt`, `help`, `static` and `VERSION`, less `INSTALL_EXCLUDE_RE` (devbin's vendored copy, each utility's `test/`, prez's crate), plus the declared build products: the prez and showreel release binaries and the crate's `Cargo.toml` (the version home of `prez.yaml`).
- The opt prefix has no default. **Question for vc:** today it is `install.prefix: ~/Devel/opt/utilz` in the committed `opt/utilz/utilz.yaml`, so every keg ships hv's path and `use opt` from any tree reads it. That is a default in all but name. I recommend `UTILZ_INSTALL_PREFIX`, set by the sleeve (Molt-matts' `vars.sh`), as Molt has `MOLT_INSTALL_PREFIX` and devbin `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX`, with the yaml key removed. The other choice keeps the yaml key, which conforms by the letter of T1 ("its config key"). Either way it is named once, in help/utilz.md's maintainer section, and unset is refused by name as now.

### T2. Publish

- **Dirty means the runtime set only.** `install_tree_state` asks `git status --porcelain -- bin opt help static VERSION` instead of the whole tree, so a live board view or an edited `intent/` file no longer blocks a publish. The built products are gitignored, so they never read as dirty.
- **Only from dev.** From opt or brew, install is refused by name, saying it runs in a dev checkout. Today an opt source is refused only as "not a git repository", which is true but does not name the rule.
- **`install --force` is the one republish.** It replaces an existing prefix only when that prefix's manifest says Utilz wrote it. An old-form manifest is Utilz's (its first row is `utilz-version`), so `install --force` republishes over one. That is the remedy T3 names, and rhadamanth's 2.10.0 opt install needs it.
- **`upgrade` no longer publishes** (T6). What goes with it: upgrade's one extra behaviour, reporting a file edited in place inside an install and keeping its install-time row instead of overwriting it (ST0014 AC08, `install_manifest_rows_preserving`). Under the contract, doctor names that drift and `install --force` overwrites it. The function and its tests are retired, and ST0014's AC08 is recorded as superseded by 0105, not re-satisfied.
- `--managed-by brew` stays as it is.

### T3. The manifest

- **Path:** `<root>/manifest.sha256`, as now (`UTILZ_MANIFEST_NAME`, one home in common.sh), named once in help/utilz.md's maintainer section.
- **Header:**
  - `# tool: utilz`
  - `# version: <VERSION>`
  - `# source_commit: <full sha>`
  - `# managed_by: utilz|brew`
  - Utilz's own keys after them: `# source_tree: <abs path>` (what makes `use dev` from opt turnkey); `# ci_state: <state>` and `# ci_detail: <run id or reason>`. The tab that joins today's `ci-state` value can't sit in a `key: value` line, so it splits in two.
  - The header keys keep their one home, now `UTILZ_MANIFEST_HEADER_KEYS`, read by the writer, the checker and the path count.
- **Body:** `<sha256>  <path>` lines in `shasum -a 256 -c` form, `LC_ALL=C sort`ed, one per runtime file.
  - The dispatcher links in `bin/` are in the body too. `shasum` hashes them through to `bin/utilz`, so a link that is missing or broken fails the body.
  - The body can no longer see a link retargeted from `utilz` to another file (AC06). git names every owned link as `bin/<name> -> utilz`, read today with no exception. So doctor's integrity check adds one structural rule: every `bin/` entry of the runtime set is a symlink whose target string is `utilz`.
  - The old `link` and `file` row kinds and their checker branches go.
- **Old form.** A manifest whose first line is not `# tool:` is not parsed as a second format. The tree function answers `opt (old manifest)` or `brew (old manifest)`, from its `managed-by` row alone, and doctor fails with the remedy: `utilz install --force` from the dev tree (opt), or `brew upgrade utilz` (brew).

### T4. Tree identity and the version line

- **The tree function.** `utilz_tree [<root>]` lives in common.sh and answers `dev`, `opt`, `brew` or `unknown`, plus the old-manifest mark, in T4's order. Its root defaults to `$UTILZ_HOME`.
  - It replaces `install_tree_kind` and `install_tree_manager`, and menuz's and the prez shim's own manifest tests. menuz's `is_install` spells `manifest.sha256` itself today, a second home for the name.
  - install's target check asks the same function of the prefix, so the running tree and a target are named by one function.
- **The version line.** `utilz --version` and `utilz version` print one line: `utilz <ver> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty]) at <abs root>`.
  - The sha is the manifest's `source_commit` in opt and brew, and HEAD in dev. `+dirty` appears in dev while the runtime set is dirty.
  - A brew root is named by its opt link, `$(brew --prefix)/opt/utilz/libexec`. It is found by the held `brew_stable_home` (banked), which checks that the link leads back to the running keg.
  - The description line and today's third line (`installed at ... (sha, CI x)`) go from the framework's answer. CI's state moves to doctor's integrity check, read from `ci_state`.
  - **Question for vc:** a utility's `--version` (`utilz:2.14.3/mdagg:1.0.0` and its description, hv's ST0015 D2 form) is not the tool's line. I'd keep it, and add the T4 line under it as its last line, so a utility's answer also says which tree replied. That last line is the one thing I'd change.
  - Doctor prints the version line at the top.

### T5. The switch

- **The link set.** It is `utilz` plus every utility of the tree, in `~/.local/bin`, declared once: `utilz_link_set <tree>` over `each_utility`. `--bin-dir` stays, documented as for tests only.
- **`use` with no word** reports each link's tree, or `brew` when no link is left and the first `utilz` on PATH resolves into the keg. It fails when the set is split across trees, or when a link is shadowed. It is shadowed when the first hit of `type -ap <name>` does not resolve into `~/.local/bin`'s resolved directory. On rhadamanth `~/bin` is a link to `~/.local/bin`, so the comparison is of resolved directories.
- **`use dev` and `use opt`** point every link of the set at that tree, refuse a tree that is not there naming the step that makes it, and then print the version line.
  - **opt's address** is the prefix (T1).
  - **dev's address** is the running tree when that is dev, and the opt manifest's `source_tree` when it is opt.
  - **From brew, `use dev` is refused** with `<checkout>/bin/utilz use dev`, because a keg's `source_tree` is brew's deleted build directory. That is today's rule, kept.
- **`use brew` removes the set:** every link in the bin dir that resolves into one of Utilz's trees (the one census walk, `install_link_census`), and nothing else. It then prints the version line that PATH now answers.
- **Shadow and split** are also doctor's PATH check, which replaces the held PATH remedy. The remedy then follows the state:
  - links present but shadowed: put `~/.local/bin` before the first Homebrew bin, which Molt-matts owns, with the shadowing path named;
  - split: `utilz use <tree>`;
  - brew with no link: brew's bin on PATH, `brew link utilz`;
  - never an exported `UTILZ_HOME`.
- **`relink` retires as a public verb.**
  - Its logic (the census, the gaps, the skip of links that aren't Utilz's, a relative `--prefix` made absolute) becomes `use`'s internals. `install_verb_relink` becomes `_install_point_links`.
  - It leaves the dispatcher's verbs and the help, and `utilz relink` is refused naming `utilz use`.
  - `relink.bats` becomes `use.bats`.
- **Nothing else repoints.** install never touches links, as now.

### T6. Upgrade by tree

`utilz upgrade` keeps its name and asks the tree function.

- **dev:** refuses a dirty runtime set, runs `git pull --ff-only`, then `cargo build --release --workspace` (`install_build_prez`, the publish's own build, so one build path). It prints the version line.
- **opt:** pulls nothing and writes nothing. It says opt is upgraded from dev with `utilz install --force`, and names dev's HEAD when it is ahead of `source_commit` (dev found by `source_tree`). It exits 2, refused with nothing changed, as Utilz's refusals do.
- **brew:** `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew upgrade utilz` when `brew outdated` names it, else it says brew's copy is current. It prints the new version line, read from the opt link.
- **unknown or old manifest:** refused, naming the T3 remedy.
- `--prefix` and `--force` leave upgrade, since it no longer publishes.

### T7

T7 is unchanged: `utilz test` is refused in opt and brew, naming the dev tree (and from a keg, a clone). Utilz has no lint verb.

### T8. The formula

- **`packaging/homebrew/utilz.rb` becomes a template.** It has one `@TAG@` and one `@REVISION@`, and a comment saying it is never installed from.
  - Its `install` is unchanged: publish into libexec with `--managed-by brew`, then link `libexec/bin/*` into bin. That is the link set, and PATH (B) keeps brew linking.
  - The caveats name `utilz use dev|opt|brew` for a maintainer with a dev checkout, and drop `relink`.
  - `test do` matches the version line: `utilz #{version} (brew, `.
- **`tools/formula-bump` becomes `tools/formula`, bash as now, with `render <tag> <out>` and `publish`.**
  - **render** keeps formula-bump's refusals: no tag, a lightweight tag, and a template without exactly one of each placeholder. It reads the commit from git and substitutes into the template. It never writes into the repo.
  - **publish** renders the newest annotated release tag into the tap's clone, `$(brew --repository)/Library/Taps/matthewsinclair/homebrew-utilz/Formula/utilz.rb`. It runs `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew audit --strict matthewsinclair/utilz/utilz`, commits, and pushes the tap.
  - `publish` pushes, so it is a verb hv types, as pushing the tap is hv's today (ST0019 WP-05).
  - `formula_bump.bats` becomes `formula.bats`. Its refusal tests move to render, and publish is tested against a scratch tap clone with a local bare remote, never the real one.

### The held docs, rewritten against the contract

- **README.md:**
  - The Installation section is the brew way in, tap, trust, install, `utilz doctor`, with `brew upgrade utilz` after. It says formulae link into brew's bin, so nothing else is needed.
  - The closing maintainer section frames dev, opt and brew from the contract and cites devbin's `docs/dev-opt-brew.md` as the shared spec. It covers `install [--force]` (the one republish), `use dev|opt|brew` ("no link means brew", and your links first on PATH), upgrade by tree, `utilz test`, generate and the manifest path.
  - The Emacs install is a symlink through the opt link, which follows each `brew upgrade`.
- **help/utilz.md:**
  - Location is the tree function's words.
  - The Quick Start is the brew pointer and `brew upgrade utilz`.
  - "Commands for a dev checkout" carries install, use and upgrade by tree, with relink gone.
  - `utilz version` shows the one-line form for each tree.
  - doctor lists the version line, the PATH check (shadow and split) and the integrity check (body, link targets, old manifest, CI state).
  - Troubleshooting follows doctor's remedies.
- **Unblocked by this half:** docs/index.md's Getting Started (brew pointer), and design-principles' Portability line and Problem 4.
- **bin/utilz's unknown-command list:** `use` becomes everyone's verb, since `use brew` is a user's way back to brew. So the list shows `help`, `doctor`, `list`, `version`, `use` and `upgrade`, then, under a line for a dev checkout, `install`, `test` and `generate`.
- **The emacs symlink:** the banked `brew_stable_home` and its one keg test come back. A dev or opt source links its own path as now.

### Tests

- **Changed:**
  - `install_lib.bats`: the runtime set, dirty on the runtime set only, and the manifest's header, body and old-form detection.
  - `install_e2e.bats`: publish, the new manifest read back with `shasum -a 256 -c`, and `--force` over an old-form opt.
  - `install_guards.bats`: refused from opt and brew by name, and refused onto a prefix that is not Utilz's.
  - `keg.bats`: the old managed-by tests become `managed_by` header tests, and `use` writes into a keg are refused.
  - `upgrade.bats`: rewritten by tree, with a scratch remote for dev's pull, a fake brew on PATH for brew's upgrade, and opt's refusal naming dev's commit.
  - `relink.bats` becomes `use.bats`: `use dev|opt|brew`, "no link means brew", shadow and split, and `relink` refused naming `use`.
  - `version_dispatch.bats`: the one-line form per tree, `+dirty`, and a brew root named by its opt link.
  - `common_lib.bats`: doctor's version line, PATH check and integrity check.
  - `formula_bump.bats` becomes `formula.bats`.
  - `menuz.bats` and `prez.bats`, where they build fake installs: the new header.
  - `dispatcher.bats`: the command list.
  - `bridge.bats`: the emacs link through the opt link on a brew-managed fake keg laid out as `<prefix>/Cellar/utilz/<v>/libexec` with `<prefix>/opt/utilz`.
- **Added:** the tree function's table (dev, opt, brew, unknown, old opt, old brew), as one test per row.
- Each changed message's test reads its words.
- The kovacs leg is dc's, on the same bytes, since the tree function, the shadow check and brew's prefix differ on Linux (`/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`).

### docs/releasing.md for the 2.14.3 cut

- **"After the cut: the Homebrew formula" becomes three steps for hv:**
  1. Publish Menuz.app's asset first, as now.
  2. Run `tools/formula publish`, which renders 2.14.3 into the tap, audits it, commits and pushes. Nothing is committed in this repository, since the template does not change per release.
  3. On rhadamanth and, through kovacs-sysadm, on kovacs, run `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew upgrade utilz`, then `utilz version`. It reads `utilz 2.14.3 (brew, <sha12>) at /opt/homebrew/opt/utilz/libexec`, at `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/utilz/libexec` on kovacs, and `utilz doctor` passes.
- **What goes:**
  - the formula-bump steps;
  - the one-time setup history's "7/7" (a count, deleted);
  - "copy the formula into the tap", since publish does it.
- The publish-before-tap ordering and the brew tag check stay.
- **T10's proof on rhadamanth goes in, as a maintainer step after the cut:** `use dev`, `use opt`, `use brew` in turn, each with the version line and doctor passing the shadow check. It needs Molt-matts' PATH change first.

### How the 2.14.2 kegs read

- **Their own doctor passes.** A 2.14.2 keg on rhadamanth or kovacs runs 2.14.2's own code, which reads its own manifest. The new doctor never runs inside it.
- **The new code reads them from another tree.** In dev or opt, `use` with no word and doctor's PATH check name the keg as `brew (old manifest)`, with the remedy `brew upgrade utilz` to 2.14.3. Doctor fails until then, as T3 says.
- After `brew upgrade utilz`, the 2.14.3 keg is written by the new install, so it carries the new header and reads as `brew`.
- **rhadamanth's 2.10.0 opt install** reads as `opt (old manifest)`, and its remedy is `utilz install --force` from the dev checkout.
- **Until Molt-matts puts `~/.local/bin` before `/opt/homebrew/bin`,** doctor's shadow check fails on rhadamanth, naming `/opt/homebrew/bin/utilz` as what shadows the dev links. That is today's state, now said rather than silent.

### Not in this half

- launchd's PATH (a sleeve decision under T5).
- Molt-matts' PATH order (Molt-matts').
- devbin's T9 reader.
- Intent.
